name: punch-out
phrase: punch out with a snap
concept: The element snaps down in scale and fades out almost instantly, like a hard punch landing. Use it for a fast, forceful dismissal with no lingering motion.

name: gut-punch
phrase: take a gut punch and collapse
concept: The element squashes flat as if struck, then rapidly shrinks away. It reads as an impact absorbing before the element gives out and disappears.

name: snap-vanish
phrase: snap and vanish
concept: The element briefly puffs up larger, then instantly collapses to nothing. The overshoot before the snap gives it a spring-loaded, decisive finish.

name: vortex-suck
phrase: get sucked into a vortex
concept: The element spins and shrinks while blurring, as if pulled down into a vortex. It suits a dramatic, swirling removal rather than a straight exit.

name: zoom-snap-out
phrase: zoom past and snap out of view
concept: The element rushes toward the viewer with a scale burst and motion blur before cutting to invisible. Use it for a fast zoom-through dismissal.

name: yeet-right
phrase: get yeeted off to the right
concept: The element is flung hard to the right with a tumbling rotation, as if thrown away with force. It is the go-to for a gleeful, abrupt good-riddance exit.

name: yeet-left
phrase: get yeeted off to the left
concept: The element is flung hard to the left with a tumbling rotation, as if thrown away with force. It is the go-to for a gleeful, abrupt good-riddance exit.

name: yeet-up
phrase: get yeeted straight up
concept: The element is flung hard upward with a tumbling rotation, as if hurled off the top of the screen. It suits an energetic, over-the-top dismissal.

name: yeet-down
phrase: get yeeted straight down
concept: The element is flung hard downward with a tumbling rotation, as if hurled off the bottom of the screen. It suits an energetic, over-the-top dismissal.

name: recoil-vanish-right
phrase: recoil back then shoot right
concept: The element pulls back left for an instant like a loaded spring, then shoots off to the right. The wind-up makes the departure feel more forceful.

name: recoil-vanish-left
phrase: recoil back then shoot left
concept: The element pulls back right for an instant like a loaded spring, then shoots off to the left. The wind-up makes the departure feel more forceful.

name: recoil-vanish-up
phrase: recoil down then shoot upward
concept: The element dips down for an instant like a loaded spring, then launches upward and out of view. The brief dip makes the upward launch feel more powerful.

name: recoil-vanish-down
phrase: recoil up then drop away
concept: The element hops up for an instant like a loaded spring, then drops hard and out of view. The brief hop makes the fall feel heavier and more sudden.

name: diagonal-blitz-ne
phrase: blitz out to the upper right
concept: The element barely moves at first, then accelerates sharply along a diagonal path up and to the right until it is gone. The sudden burst of speed reads as urgent.

name: diagonal-blitz-nw
phrase: blitz out to the upper left
concept: The element barely moves at first, then accelerates sharply along a diagonal path up and to the left until it is gone. The sudden burst of speed reads as urgent.

name: diagonal-blitz-se
phrase: blitz out to the lower right
concept: The element barely moves at first, then accelerates sharply along a diagonal path down and to the right until it is gone. The sudden burst of speed reads as urgent.

name: diagonal-blitz-sw
phrase: blitz out to the lower left
concept: The element barely moves at first, then accelerates sharply along a diagonal path down and to the left until it is gone. The sudden burst of speed reads as urgent.

name: spin-shrink-out
phrase: spin rapidly and shrink away
concept: The element spins through several fast rotations while shrinking to nothing. It suits a whirlwind, almost cartoonish removal from the screen.

name: spin-shrink-out-reverse
phrase: spin the other way and shrink away
concept: The element spins through several fast counterclockwise rotations while shrinking to nothing. It gives the same whirlwind removal with the opposite spin direction.

name: corkscrew-out
phrase: corkscrew away and disappear
concept: The element spins tightly while drifting diagonally downward and shrinking, like a corkscrew boring out of view. It combines rotation and travel for a busier exit.

name: spiral-flick
phrase: flick into a spiral overhead
concept: The element spins loosely while drifting upward and fading, like it was flicked away into the air. It is lighter and airier than a hard spin-shrink.

name: blast-off
phrase: blast off in a burst
concept: The element flashes larger with a glowing shockwave ring, then rapidly collapses to nothing, like a small explosion running in reverse. Reserve it for a rare, high-impact dismissal.

name: implosion-out
phrase: implode into nothing
concept: The element brightens and grows for a moment, then rapidly shrinks and blurs to nothing, like light collapsing inward. It gives a punchy exit without shadow effects.

name: flare-vanish
phrase: flare bright then vanish
concept: The element flickers rapidly like a flare catching, then cuts to nothing. The flicker beforehand makes the disappearance feel electric and abrupt.

name: jolt-slide-right
phrase: jolt side to side then slide right
concept: The element jitters left and right rapidly as if startled, then slides fast off to the right. The jolt sells a moment of surprise before the getaway.

name: jolt-slide-left
phrase: jolt side to side then slide left
concept: The element jitters left and right rapidly as if startled, then slides fast off to the left. The jolt sells a moment of surprise before the getaway.

name: jolt-slide-up
phrase: jolt up and down then slide up
concept: The element jitters up and down rapidly as if startled, then slides fast off the top of the view. The jolt sells a moment of surprise before the getaway.

name: jolt-slide-down
phrase: jolt up and down then slide down
concept: The element jitters up and down rapidly as if startled, then slides fast off the bottom of the view. The jolt sells a moment of surprise before the getaway.

name: tilt-snap-right
phrase: tilt sharply and snap out to the right
concept: The element tilts hard on its axis in an instant, then snaps away to the right. The sudden tilt makes the exit feel off-balance and abrupt.

name: tilt-snap-left
phrase: tilt sharply and snap out to the left
concept: The element tilts hard on its axis in an instant, then snaps away to the left. The sudden tilt makes the exit feel off-balance and abrupt.

name: skew-slam-right
phrase: skew hard and slam out to the right
concept: The element skews sharply as if slammed sideways, then shoots off to the right. Skew instead of rotation gives it a harder, more mechanical snap.

name: skew-slam-left
phrase: skew hard and slam out to the left
concept: The element skews sharply as if slammed sideways, then shoots off to the left. Skew instead of rotation gives it a harder, more mechanical snap.

name: skew-slam-down
phrase: skew down and slam away
concept: The element shears vertically and drops straight down fast, like it was slammed downward through a gap. It reads heavier and more sudden than a sideways skew.

name: reel-back-snap
phrase: reel back then snap off diagonally
concept: The element pulls back and skews the opposite way like a slingshot loading, then snaps off diagonally at speed. The wind-up telegraphs the sudden release.

name: ejector-seat
phrase: eject straight up and out
concept: The element launches straight upward at speed with a slight rotation, like an ejector seat firing. It suits an urgent, vertical emergency-style exit.

name: slingshot-out
phrase: pull back and let a slingshot fly
concept: The element pulls back and shrinks slightly as though drawn back in a slingshot, then releases forward with a stretch as it shoots off. The elastic release feels satisfying and quick.

name: rug-pull
phrase: get the rug pulled out
concept: The element drops straight down fast with a slight rotation, as if the ground vanished beneath it. It works well for a sudden, unfair-feeling removal.

name: trapdoor-drop
phrase: fall through a trapdoor
concept: The element drops straight down and shrinks slightly as it accelerates, like falling through a trapdoor. It stays upright, unlike a rug pull, for a cleaner vertical fall.

name: kick-out-right
phrase: get kicked out to the right
concept: The element compresses as if struck by a kick, then rockets off to the right while rotating. The squash-then-launch pairing reads as a forceful shove.

name: kick-out-left
phrase: get kicked out to the left
concept: The element compresses as if struck by a kick, then rockets off to the left while rotating. The squash-then-launch pairing reads as a forceful shove.

name: catapult-arc-right
phrase: catapult up and over to the right
concept: The element launches upward, arcs across, and drops away to the right, tracing a catapult's path. The curved trajectory makes it read as thrown rather than slid.

name: catapult-arc-left
phrase: catapult up and over to the left
concept: The element launches upward, arcs across, and drops away to the left, tracing a catapult's path. The curved trajectory makes it read as thrown rather than slid.

name: dropkick-diagonal
phrase: get dropkicked off at an angle
concept: The element spins a sharp half turn while rocketing diagonally downward, as if dropkicked off the screen. One hard rotation keeps it punchier than a multi-spin exit.

name: bounce-eject-up
phrase: bounce once then eject upward
concept: The element dips down briefly as if compressing, then rockets straight up and away. The small bounce first gives the launch a coiled, springboard feel.

name: bounce-eject-down
phrase: bounce once then eject downward
concept: The element hops up briefly as if compressing, then drops hard straight down and away. The small bounce first gives the drop a coiled, springboard feel.

name: rapid-fire-out
phrase: judder rapidly then vanish
concept: The element stutters through several quick side-to-side jolts before cutting out entirely. The rapid judder feels glitchy and urgent rather than smooth.

name: whip-crack-out
phrase: whip-crack and snap away
concept: The element rotates sharply past its final angle and springs back slightly before vanishing, like the crack of a whip. The overshoot-and-settle rotation makes the exit feel sharp and elastic.

name: flick-up-arc
phrase: flick up in a light arc
concept: The element is flicked upward and drifts slightly sideways as it fades, tracing a light arc rather than a heavy launch. It suits a quick, effortless dismissal.

name: flick-down-arc
phrase: flick down in a light arc
concept: The element is flicked downward and drifts slightly sideways as it fades, tracing a light arc rather than a heavy drop. It suits a quick, effortless dismissal.

name: gone-in-a-blink
phrase: collapse shut in a blink
concept: The element collapses vertically to a thin line first, then squeezes horizontally to nothing, like a shutter blinking closed. The two-stage collapse reads as a fast mechanical close rather than a fade.
keywords: collapse to a line then gone
